editorial.headline: Bali’s Bag-Retail Paradox
editorial.standfirst: This specialist retail activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium closes the registration route on the island.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this retail activity in Bali today, even though it is nationally open to foreign ownership. The island-wide Bali moratorium blocks PMA registration for activities assessed at Low or Medium-Low risk; at the Besar scale, every scope in this activity falls within those bands. That result is not a question of product mix or a discretionary local reading. It follows from the recorded risk classification and applies permanently across the province. For founders considering a Bali vehicle, the first practical fact is therefore the restriction itself: national openness does not create a Bali PMA registration route while this moratorium governs it.

Nationally, this is specialist retail for bags, wallets, suitcases, backpacks and related goods. Its material range is deliberately broad: leather, imitation leather, textiles, plastic, rubber and other materials all sit within the activity. The retail offer may encompass handbags, shopping bags, school bags, document bags and sports bags, alongside wallets, cosmetics cases, knife or sword sheaths, camera and eyewear cases, and pencil cases. Umbrella retail is included as well. The common thread is a dedicated retail activity for carrying, storing and protecting personal belongings, rather than a narrow retail format defined by one material or one product style.

The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the commercial concept can be framed across the full listed scale range, from a modest specialist shop to a larger operation. It does not, however, alter the Bali position for PMA: the recorded finding at the Besar scale is Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope, bringing the activity within the province-wide moratorium. Scale availability and PMA registrability in Bali are therefore separate questions in this record.

At national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, under the cited Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In Bali, the decisive condition is the permanent rule blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, supported here by Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The clean reading is neither a hidden cap nor a conditional workaround: full foreign ownership is nationally permitted, while Bali PMA registration for this activity is blocked.
